headline: Segmentation and normalization methods refine brain single-cell and spatial profiling
label: Brain Single Cell Spatial Analysis
summary: Segmentation accuracy and normalization choices in brain single-cell and spatial data now bear directly on Alzheimer's-related inference.
synthesis: The common thread is methodological work on brain single-cell and spatial data in which upstream steps, namely cell segmentation and count normalization, shape downstream biological inference. SPInfer fine-tunes Cellpose-SAM for brain tissue segmentation, raising F1 from 0.37 to 0.84, and reports that zero-shot versus fine-tuned masks change Alzheimer's-related analysis. A new normalization for snRNA-seq and multiome data links neuronal mitochondrial biogenesis suppression to Alzheimer's dementia, while CEP-IP with CMRF identifies a mitochondrial MT-CO3 co-expression module in SEA-AD microglia linked to cognition, with an R package released. SpaceDX jointly tests differential expression and spatial localization, and ATLAS profiles 40M cells across mouse brains using scRNA-seq-derived probe signatures. The emphasis is on upstream analytic steps as determinants of results rather than single-assay novelty. The NDD gene and organ-specific proteomic aging clock items extend the framing to neurodevelopment and multi-organ aging.
